answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before transacting, like a harbor charging every vessel a berthing bond. One honest agent pays once; an attacker spinning up a thousand sock-puppets must fund a thousand bonds, and any identity caught double-signing or copying another agent's work loses its stake. The bond is basalt-solid collateral, not a password: cheap to verify, ruinous to fake at scale, and the lagoon of honest trade stays open because legitimate newcomers can always earn their bond back by behaving well.
